sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ | kṛtaṃ vai sakalaṃ kāryaṃ yajñā no rakṣitāstvayā | yadi deyo varo'smākaṃ tvayā cāsuramarddini || 20 || asminsthāne sadā tiṣṭha munīnāṃ hitakāmyayā | kaṃṭakāḥ śoṣitā daityāstena kaṃṭakaśoṣiṇī | adyaprabhṛti nāmāstu tena devi sadā tviha || 21 ||
english: 20-21. O goddess, O suppressor of Asuras, all our tasks have been accomplished. Our Yajñas were saved by you. If at all any boon is to be given, do stay here in this holy spot with a desire for the welfare of the sages. The thorns, in the form of the Daityas, have been squeezed dry. Hence, O goddess, this ‘Kaṇṭaka-Śoṣaṇī’ (the destroyer of thorns) shall be your permanent name from now onwards.
